findings.title: FrameReplayMarker::mark_and_check_frame has a TOCTOU race between get + put (separate redb transactions)

evidence.caps_code: crates/benten-caps/src/chain_authority.rs:404-421 — mark_and_check_frame calls self.backend.get(&key) then conditionally self.backend.put(&key, &[]). Two separate calls.
evidence.backend_code: crates/benten-graph/src/redb_backend.rs:2956-2970 — KVBackend::get opens a read_txn; KVBackend::put opens a SEPARATE write_txn. There is no compare-and-set / atomic-mark operation on the KVBackend trait.
evidence.engine_caller: crates/benten-engine/src/engine.rs:1524-1547 — apply_atrium_merge invokes the marker without any per-zone or per-engine serializing lock around the marker call
evidence.attack_class: two concurrent apply_atrium_merge invocations presenting the SAME inbound session_nonce both observe already=false and both pass the F3 replay defense

findings.attack_surface: F3 anti-replay seam is racy. An adversary who can drive two concurrent inbound frames carrying the same session_nonce (e.g. two parallel iroh connections delivering replayed frames at the same time, OR a single inbound frame ingested via two distinct apply_atrium_merge tasks) can defeat the durable replay marker. Compromise #23 promises 'anti-replay re-homed, not dropped' — at HEAD it IS re-homed but racy. The ephemeral verify step-(3) freshness gate also cannot catch concurrent presentations; F3 IS the load-bearing defense for in-window replay and currently has no atomicity.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW — either (a) extend KVBackend trait with a typed compare_and_insert(key, value) -> Result<bool, _> method (returning whether the insert created the entry) AND change mark_and_check_frame to use it, OR (b) route the marker call through GraphBackend::transaction(|tx| ...) so both the get + put run inside one txn (the existing transaction API supports this), OR (c) document a serializing per-engine lock around the apply_atrium_merge marker call. Option (b) is lowest-cost (existing surface; ~10 LOC change inside mark_and_check_frame to wrap the get+put in a transaction).

findings.title: No peer/principal policy gate exists to REQUIRE PQ-hybrid (reject classical-only-downgrade arm) at envelope verification — silent acceptance of 0x6400 by policy

evidence.dispatcher_code: crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/codepoint.rs:240-253 — CipherSuiteCodepoint::resolve() returns Ok(()) for BOTH 0x647a (hybrid default) AND 0x6400 (classical-only downgrade). Both are 'live' arms.
evidence.absence_of_policy: grep across all crates for 'require.*hybrid|enforce.*hybrid|policy.*pq|disallow.*classical' yields ZERO production sites — there is no peer-side / engine-config / capability-policy mechanism to express 'reject any envelope sealed under 0x6400 / 0x6400-derived keys' as a policy
evidence.freeze_doc_claim: V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md item 6 line 478 frames 0x6400 as 'LIVE, non-default classical-only downgrade' but offers NO surface for a consumer to reject it
evidence.scope: CLAUDE.md baked-in #5 PQ-hybrid-default reframe: hybrid IS the v1-beta default + the swap matrix supports classical-only as a non-default downgrade. The downgrade defense via swap-matrix construction (typed try_pure_pq_sole_trust_path / explicit constructor) covers the producer side; there is NO consumer-side policy to enforce 'I won't accept content sealed under the classical-only arm'

findings.attack_surface: A coerced or hostile peer can produce all content under 0x6400 (classical-only); recipients have NO policy mechanism to reject it on hybrid-required grounds. The classical-only construction is still cryptographically sound BY ITSELF (Ed25519 + X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305) — so this isn't an immediate compromise — but it does mean the platform cannot enforce 'PQ-hybrid is mandatory' at the verify-side, which contradicts the marketing posture of CLAUDE.md baked-in #5 'PQ-hybrid IS the v1-beta DEFAULT' for consumers who think 'default = enforced'. The harvest-now-decrypt-later property (baked-in #5 + #18) is silently lost on any 0x6400-sealed content.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW lite — add a per-engine config flag CryptoPolicy::require_hybrid_pq: bool (default true at v1-beta per the reframe ratification) consulted at unwrap / verify entry points; rejecting 0x6400 envelopes when set with typed ErrorCode::DowngradeArmRejectedByPolicy. Tracked at SECURITY-POSTURE.md as a clarification that the swap-matrix downgrade arms are PRODUCER-side; consumer-side policy is needed for the 'hybrid mandatory' marketing posture. If the orchestrator deems this scope-bleed past G-CORE-9 FREEZE, DEFER-NAMED-NOW into Phase-4-Meta-Composing v1-assessment-window with the explicit destination + an SECURITY-POSTURE.md row acknowledging 0x6400 is silently accepted at recipient at v1-beta.

findings.title: graph-AEAD seam (make_key_material_matching) trusts attacker-controlled envelope cipher_codepoint when constructing the AeadKeyMaterial

evidence.graph_code: crates/benten-graph/src/aead_wrap.rs:507-526 — make_key_material_matching reads codepoint from envelope (attacker-controlled bytes via from_wire_bytes) and labels the caller's raw 32-B key with that codepoint via AeadKeyMaterial::from_raw_bytes. The downstream cipher-suite unwrap (aead.rs:288) typed-rejects on key.codepoint != envelope.cipher_codepoint — but they are now equal BY CONSTRUCTION because the helper threaded the envelope's codepoint into the key.
evidence.docstring_acknowledges: Line 500-506 — 'this helper threads the envelope's codepoint into the key newtype so a caller that presents the *correct* key for an envelope sealed under a non-default codepoint (e.g. 0x6400 classical-only X25519 downgrade arm) gets through' — explicit acknowledgement that the codepoint-mismatch defense is bypassed at this seam
evidence.natural_defense_dependency: the practical defense reduces to: if the attacker swaps the cipher_codepoint byte, K_root derivation under 0x647a-vs-0x6400 yields different bytes (different upstream encapsulation paths) → ChaCha20-Poly1305 auth fails. This works at v1-beta because both arms feed into ChaCha20-Poly1305 with codepoint-distinct K_root values. The defense is INCIDENTAL to the construction, not structurally explicit.

findings.attack_surface: An attacker who mutates the envelope's cipher_codepoint byte (e.g. 0x647a → 0x6400) at any in-transit byte does NOT trip the cipher-suite layer's codepoint-mismatch defense — the graph-AEAD layer re-labels the key to match. The natural backstop is that K_root differs between the two wrap paths; but this is brittle: any future swap-matrix arm whose K_root happens to collide with another arm's K_root (e.g. two arms that derive K_root via the same X-Wing-combiner with slightly different inputs) would re-open the silent-downgrade vector. The codepoint should be derivation-bound to the K_root via the structural_kdf info-tags (currently info-tag is 'root'/'step' only — does NOT include the cipher-suite codepoint).
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW lite — either (a) extend structural_kdf::derive_root info-tag to include the cipher-suite codepoint binding (e.g. info = 'root:codepoint:<le_bytes>' || root_cid) — wire-format coupling but cheap (~5 LOC + golden test for backward-compat); OR (b) at make_key_material_matching, reject envelopes whose codepoint does not match an expected codepoint passed in by the caller (additive API; existing callers that don't care can pass None). Option (a) is structurally cleaner and provides defense in depth at the KDF level. If neither lands at G-CORE-9 freeze, register an explicit OBS in SECURITY-POSTURE.md acknowledging the codepoint-binding gap relies on K_root accidental codepoint-uniqueness.
